🚨 MIKROTIK “MIKROTRICK”: UNAUTH SSH CHAIN TO FULL ADMIN — EXPLOITED BEFORE PATCHES  CERT Polska published a 22 Sep 2026 technical analysis of MikroTrick, the unauthenticated MikroTik RouterOS SSH takeover chain combining CVE-2026-67279 (rekey state-machine flaw) with CVE-2026-86060 (username “-2” / login argv injection) for full admin without password or SSH key.  • Patches: RouterOS 6.49.21, 7.23.4, 7.24.2, 7.25beta3 (vendor released ~3 Sep 2026) • CERT Polska says logs matching the chain (failed login for user -2, privileged “ops” account) appeared as early as 2 Sep — before patches • Distinctive IoCs: login failure for user -2; creation of fully privileged ops; connections from 82.192.72.4 in public reports; Flagged/device-mode checks after update • CVE-2026-86060 added to CISA KEV (10 Sep) with short remediation window • CERT incorrectly notes some coverage mixed in CVE-2026-67276 (separate RSA-forge path) — MikroTrick is the 67279+86060 pair • Immediate: patch, restrict public SSH, hunt -2 / ops / unknown config changes per MikroTik security bulletin  ⚠️ Analyst Note:  Primary is CERT Polska’s own technical write-up (not The Hacker News / Telegram CTI). Exploitation evidence is from CERT coordination plus public admin logs; treat as confirmed vulnerable-device attacks against internet-exposed SSH, not a new zero-day today.  We assess MikroTrick as a confirmed, previously exploited RouterOS admin-takeover chain — patch and hunt now if not already done.  Primary (CERT Polska, 22 Sep 2026): cert.pl/en/posts/2026/09/mik…  Also: cert.pl/en/posts/2026/09/vul… #DDW #MikroTik #MikroTrick #RouterOS #KEV #ThreatIntelligence #CyberSecurity

🚨 GITLAB ISSUE-BY-EMAIL TOKEN CAN PUSH TO MAIN AND BYPASS IP ALLOWLISTS  Aikido Security (Joe Leon) published research today showing that GitLab’s per-user “incoming email” / issue-by-email address embeds a long-lived account token. Anyone who obtains that address can act as the victim over email — including paths that land commits on protected branches and run CI/CD — even when browser/git access is blocked by IP restrictions.  • Address looks like a project bug-report mailbox but the embedded token is account-wide • Sender address is not verified; any mailbox that knows the address can trigger actions • Swap -issue for -merge-request and attach a git .patch → GitLab can apply changes (including .gitlab-ci.yml) and run jobs • Confirmed against projects behind IP allowlists: email path still accepted while HTTP/SSH were blocked • Affects GitLab.com and self-managed instances with incoming email enabled; no user toggle to disable • GitLab treated the report as intended behavior; UI copy was updated, but the mail-token mechanism remains • Defenders: rotate Incoming email token (Personal access tokens), treat published glimt- addresses as secrets, do not treat IP allowlists as absolute  ⚠️ Analyst Note:  This is a researcher design/defaults finding (HackerOne closed as intended behavior), not a numbered CVE patch advisory. Risk depends on role of the leaked token’s owner and whether the address was published or otherwise exposed.  We assess this as confirmed Aikido research on an abuse path in GitLab incoming email — not confirmation of mass in-the-wild exploitation.  Primary (Aikido Security, 23 Sep 2026): aikido.dev/blog/gitlab-email… #DDW #GitLab #DevSecOps #CI_CD #SupplyChain #ThreatIntelligence #CyberSecurity

Named large victims are described without public identifiers in the report; treat card/skimmer counts as researcher tallies under investigation, not victim confirmations.  We assess this as a confirmed researcher-documented ecommerce intrusion/skimmer campaign with verified exfiltration and in-the-wild skimmers, still active. 🇺🇸🚨 ASTRANA HEALTH FILES MATERIAL CYBER INCIDENT AFTER SOCIAL-ENGINEERING ACCESS  Astrana Health (NASDAQ: ASTH) disclosed in an SEC Form 8-K that its subsidiary Astrana Health Management detected unauthorized activity after threat actors spoofed the company’s main corporate phone number and impersonated personnel to socially engineer employee access.  • Materiality determined as of September 22, 2026 (Item 1.05) • Company believes certain private and/or confidential information on its servers was accessed and/or acquired without authorization • Scope still under investigation — including whether patient, employee, provider, business, financial, or IP data was affected • Response so far: credential resets, restricted remote-access tools, restores from clean backups, enhanced monitoring; third-party forensics engaged • Law enforcement notified; regulators and payer partners being notified; required patient notices to follow findings • Company currently does not expect a material effect on financial condition or results of operations  ⚠️ Analyst Note:  This is a company SEC disclosure, not a dark-web leak listing. Patient and other data impact remain undetermined in the filing — do not treat “1.5M+ patients” market framing as confirmed exfiltration volume.  We assess this as a confirmed material incident disclosure by Astrana, with investigation ongoing as to what categories of data (if any) left the environment. 🚨 CPANEL CVE-2026-87899: CALDAV/CARDDAV PATH TO ROOT ON SHARED HOSTING  cPanel / WebPros published an official security advisory for CVE-2026-87899 in cPanel’s CalDAV/CardDAV stack (disclosed September 22, 2026).  An authenticated cPanel account holder can escalate via CalDAV/CardDAV to code execution as root, giving full server control. The issue affects cPanel/WHM v120 or later and is especially relevant for shared hosting, where any customer account is enough — WHM admin access is not required.  Fixed builds include 11.134.0.57+, 11.136.0.41+, 11.138.0.8+, and WP Squared 11.138.1.11+.  ⚠️ Analyst Note: The vendor advisory does not claim known in-the-wild exploitation, and this CVE was not listed in CISA KEV as of our check. Treat as a high-priority patching item for hosting providers and anyone running affected cPanel/WHM builds. Credit: Ali Mustafa (rz1027).  Related same-day official cPanel CalDAV/CardDAV and WP Toolkit advisories exist (CVE-2026-68490, CVE-2026-87900); this post focuses on the root-escalation path.  Primary: support.cpanel.net/hc/en-us/… #DDW #cPanel #CVE202687899 #WebHosting #PrivilegeEscalation #RCE #ThreatIntelligence #CyberSecurity

On a recent Incident response case, we encountered VMkatz.  "It extracts Windows secrets - NTLM hashes, DPAPI master keys, Kerberos tickets, cached domain credentials, LSA secrets, NTDS.dit, BitLocker keys - directly from VM memory snapshots and virtual disks, on the NAS, the hypervisor, wherever the VM files are." [1]  Defender detected it with the following signature: VirTool:Win64/Vekesz.A  The out-of-the-box release from the GitHub page is also heavily flagged, but one could compile (and obfuscate) the code to stay under the radar. In our case, the attacker just disabled real-time monitoring and added an exclusion:  Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring $true Add-MpPreference -ExclusionPath "C:\"  And then pointing it to a directory, "and let it find everything", as pointed out in the documentation.  ./vmkatz.exe C:\ClusterStorage\CSV01\node-002\  I think monitoring for AV alerts (and exclusions!) could go a long way. The basics make the difference. ☝️  [1] github.com/nikaiw/VMkatz
